::: {.about-flex-main}
My background is in statistical physics: finding structure in systems that
are large, noisy, and only partially observable. During my PhD I worked on
community detection in complex networks, extreme value statistics, and
synchronization in nonlinear dynamical systems — problems where the honest
answer is a distribution, not a point estimate, and where getting the
uncertainty right matters as much as getting the estimate right.

That same discipline is what draws me to quantitative finance. Credit risk,
derivatives pricing, and factor research all come down to the same core
problem: build a model that is precise enough to be useful, honest about
what it doesn't know, and robust when the data stops behaving the way your
assumptions assumed it would.
:::

## How I work

I like problems that sit at the boundary between rigorous theory and messy
real-world data — extreme value theory applied to tail risk, uncertainty
quantification applied to model validation, network methods applied to
systemic risk. I write my own tooling rather than treating models as black
boxes, because being able to explain *why* a model says what it says is
usually the difference between a model that survives model risk review and
one that doesn't.

I'm currently looking for roles in quantitative research, model validation,
and model risk — credit risk, market risk, or systematic equity research.
